raw_response:
I am old now, 73, and only one person in the house, so I cannot spread myself too thin. On my 3 mu, I will still do what is familiar and steady. I will keep 2 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because grain is safer and I know this land well. The other 1 mu I will put to cotton, same as some years before, so if grain price is not good I still have another income. I only finished primary school, so I do not count things too finely. I mostly follow what worked before and what I see nearby. Wheat cannot be too thin on fertilizer or it turns yellow and yield falls. Maize after wheat has a tight window, so I keep the work simple and fast. Cotton takes more hand work, but on 1 mu I can still manage it myself. Water from the well costs money, so I will irrigate when the crop really needs it, not too many times. I would rather spend a bit on fertilizer for the wheat and maize than risk empty ears, but I still must keep some cash in hand because I am alone and cannot afford trouble.
